rationale: The differential shows golden_rejected: the golden submission (which correctly names only u_perm_nand3 as the suspect instance, per hidden_spec.ground_truth) fails SR3 because evaluate.py's ground-truth suspect computation uses a flip-sensitivity/taint analysis over the netlist that implicates 13 additional instances (inverters, correction NAND/NOR stages, output-stage gates) that merely sit on the signal path propagating the divergence, rather than being the causal locus of the behavioral defect. This is a genuine evaluator bug: it grades suspect_instances against an overly broad structural/propagation-based ground truth instead of the intended single-instance causal ground truth. Because golden acceptance fails, mutation testing never proceeds (mutation_status=blocked_by_differential), so mutation_score=0.0 and discrimination_coverage=0.0 are not meaningful on their own but block retention regardless. The netlist artifact itself also has a severe leak issue (verbose first-person scratch reasoning revealing the exact bug design embedded directly in inputs/perm_cone_netlist.v), but that is secondary to the blocking golden_rejected defect, which must be fixed first per precedence rules. I am flagging evaluation_framework as the primary artifact to revise since golden_rejected is the blocking failure class; the leak issue should be raised in a follow-up round once the evaluator is fixed.
revision_instructions:
evaluate.py's SR3 check currently computes a broad flip-sensitivity/signal-propagation set from the netlist and requires suspect_instances to be a superset of that entire set, which incorrectly fails a correct submission that names only the single instance that is the actual behavioral root cause of the divergence. Rewrite the SR3 ground-truth computation so it identifies the minimal causal instance(s) whose local logic function differs from what the reference specification requires at that point in the cone -- not every downstream gate that merely propagates the resulting signal change to the output. Concretely: for each candidate gate instance, compute what its output value SHOULD be if it were correctly implementing the documented reference behavior, and flag only instances whose actual simulated output diverges from that expected local value at the failing input vector; do not flag instances whose own local truth table is correct but which happen to sit downstream of a divergent signal. The check must PASS when suspect_instances contains exactly the root-cause instance(s) by this local-correctness definition, and must still FAIL on submissions that omit the true root-cause instance or that name only unrelated instances. Verify by re-running the differential: the golden submission (which names exactly one instance corresponding to the true single miswired gate) must now pass SR3, while the naive baseline (empty suspect_instances) must still fail SR3. Also flag for a follow-up pass (do not block this fix): inputs/perm_cone_netlist.v contains leftover first-person design-reasoning prose and undefined macro references preceding the module declaration that leak the intended bug location to participants and cause iverilog warnings -- these must eventually be stripped so the file contains only the clean synthesizable module, but this is not required to unblock the evaluator fix.
Separately, also note: only after golden acceptance is fixed and confirmed passing, mutation testing should be re-run so mutation_score and requirement_discrimination_coverage_score become meaningful metrics.
